answer: Admission runs through a narrow inlet: one identity per block, each admission hashing the one before, so a batch of k takes k blocks and cannot be parallelized. Each applicant locks a copper bond vesting after twelve blocks, and each admitted identity carries an umber mark, a non-transferable hash of its position in the admission chain. Contiguous admissions share a mark family, and the ledger weights a family by the square root of its size, so a farm entering in one run is visible and earns one share. Honest agents arrive scattered in time; a sybil arrives as a row.
